recognize_zh: 數顆淋巴球的卵圓形核染色質緻密，細胞質往兩極延伸成尖細尾巴，呈紡錘形（fusiform）且有極性的細胞質突起；背景紅血球普遍皺縮成棘狀。
features: Several small to medium lymphoid cells with oval nuclei and dense chromatin
Bipolar tapering pale-blue cytoplasmic projections giving a spindle (fusiform) shape
Background crenated (echinocytic) red cells, likely artifact; one small round lymphocyte and scattered platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood film (Leishman) shows several small to medium-sized lymphoid cells with oval nuclei, condensed chromatin, and scant pale cytoplasm drawn out into polar tapering projections, producing a spindle-shaped appearance. Nucleoli are not appreciable and the cytoplasm lacks granules. Red cells show diffuse crenation, likely a preparation artifact. In a patient with massive splenomegaly, circulating lymphoid cells with polarized cytoplasmic projections are suggestive of splenic marginal zone lymphoma; immunophenotyping and splenic or bone marrow histology are needed for confirmation.

ddx.vs: Hairy cells show circumferential rather than polar projections, abundant pale cytoplasm, and CD25/CD103/CD123/annexin A1 positivity.

ddx.dx: Splenic diffuse red pulp small B-cell lymphoma
ddx.vs: SDRPL cells have broad-based polar villi and morphology overlapping SMZL, requiring splenic histology showing red pulp rather than white pulp involvement.
HCL-variant cells have a prominent central nucleolus and are CD103 positive but CD25 negative.
Artifactual spindling occurs in thick dragged areas and lacks true villi, so it should be judged in well-spread monolayer areas.
